headline: AI rout sends S&P into correction: Treasuries rally 12–15bp, gold sinks 2.4%, oil edges up
summary: A deepening AI-led equity sell-off, with the Nasdaq down 5.3% and Nvidia 13.8%, drove a broad flight to bonds: the US 2-year fell about 14bp and the German 10-year about 9.5bp as 50bp Fed hike bets were dropped. Gold and silver still fell another 2.4% and 3.8% as investors sold metals to raise cash, ending gold's worst week since March. Oil ended slightly higher as Hormuz mine attacks, Houthi threats to Saudi ports and pre-holiday short covering offset surplus worries, but still fell for a third week.
drivers: AI sell-off drives a haven bid for bonds

The S&P 500 fell 3.7% into correction territory and the Nasdaq 5.3% as Nvidia dropped 13.8% on an SEC accounting probe and chip stocks fell 10.7%. The US 2-year fell about 14bp to near 4.64% and the 10-year about 12bp to near 4.93%, back below 5%.

Money markets unwound bets on a half-point December hike but still price about 91–99% odds of 25bp despite Cook arguing policy is not restrictive enough. Final UMich one-year inflation expectations fell to 3.7% from 4.7% in October, helping the rally.

Spot gold fell about 2.4% to near $3,538 after touching $3,502.93, ending the week down about 8.7%, and silver lost 3.8% to near $41.22 as investors sold metals to cover equity losses. The dollar index was flat near 103.9, so the selling was about raising cash, not the currency.
Oil bounces on Gulf risk but posts a third weekly loss

Dec WTI settled 77¢ higher at $83.98 at expiry and Brent 59¢ higher at $92.57 on Hormuz mine strikes, Houthi threats to Saudi ports and short covering before Thanksgiving. WTI still fell 5.2% on the week as Hormuz flows are back near pre-war levels.

oil.note: Dec WTI settled +77¢ (+0.9%) at $83.98 at expiry after dipping near $81.6; Brent +59¢ at $92.57. WTI −5.2% on the week.
oil.why: Crude recovered from an early drop of almost 2% as traders added risk premium before the Thanksgiving week: Iran said two tankers struck mines and burned in Hormuz, attacks on tankers are running near one a day in November, and the Houthis threatened Saudi Red Sea ports after firing at Riyadh. Short covering into Dec WTI expiry helped. The bounce stayed small because Hormuz exports are back near pre-war levels and the AI sell-off raised demand worries.
oil.outlook: Bias sideways to lower in an $80–88 range while surplus expectations dominate; a settle under $81.5 opens the high $70s. Verified loss of Gulf or Russian barrels, or OPEC+ restraint on Nov 29, would bring $88–90 back.
oil.watch: US-Iran and Hormuz headlines, EIA stocks Wed Nov 25, thin Thanksgiving trading and OPEC+ Nov 29.

gas.note: Dec RBOB rose 0.76¢ (+0.3%) to $2.5027, a second small gain, but fell 4.5% on the week and 24% in three weeks.
gas.why: Gasoline edged up with crude as Gulf attack headlines and pre-holiday short covering lifted the energy complex, while diesel futures slipped about 0.3%. Gains were limited by ample supply after last week's 5.2m-barrel gasoline build and weaker risk appetite. The three-week fall of about 81¢ is the steepest since March 2020, and AAA's pump average fell to about $3.68, 19¢ lower in a week and 59¢ below a month ago.
gas.outlook: Bias sideways to lower in a $2.38–2.60 range with winter-grade fuel and rising stocks; a move above $2.60 would need WTI above $88 or a refinery outage.
gas.watch: EIA stocks Wed Nov 25, AAA's Thanksgiving average Nov 26 and the Dec contract's Nov 30 expiry.

gold.note: Spot fell about 2.4% (−$87) to near $3,538 after a low of $3,502.93, ending the week down about 8.7%.
gold.why: Gold kept falling even though Treasury yields dropped 12–15bp and the dollar was flat, which shows the driver was forced selling: the Nasdaq fell 5.3% and the S&P 500 entered a correction, so investors sold profitable metal positions to cover losses and margin calls. A fully priced 25bp Fed hike on Dec 9, with about 70bp of hikes priced into 2027, keeps the cost of holding gold high. Analysts noted the dip toward $3,500 drew some late buying.
gold.outlook: Bias still lower but stretched, in a $3,450–3,650 range; a weekly close under $3,500 targets $3,430–3,450, while a close above Friday's high near $3,637 would signal a bottom.
gold.watch: Equity stability, Fed speakers and the dollar in a thin Thanksgiving week; US data before the Dec 9 Fed.

silver.note: Spot dropped about 3.8% to near $41.22 after touching $40.99, down more than 15% on the week.
silver.why: Silver fell faster than gold because it suffers both from the deleveraging and from growth worries: chip stocks fell 10.7% and copper about 3%, hurting the industrial-demand story for solar and electronics. Tighter Fed policy and forced selling to cover equity losses added pressure. The gold-silver ratio stayed near 85, showing silver's extra weakness, and the old $50 high gave no support on the way down.
silver.outlook: Bias lower in a $39–44 range; a close below $41 opens about $40.3 and then $39. Stabilising chip stocks and copper would be needed to regain $42.8–44.
silver.watch: Chip-stock moves, copper and the dollar into Thanksgiving week.

us2y.note: Down about 14bp to near 4.64%, the biggest one-day fall in months, led by safe-haven buying.
us2y.why: The front end rallied hardest as the stock rout tightened financial conditions and traders dropped bets on a 50bp December hike; a 25bp move is still about 91–99% priced. Gov. Cook said policy is not restrictive enough, but markets read rising growth risk as a reason for a slower path. UMich one-year inflation expectations fell to 3.7% from 4.7% in October.
us2y.outlook: Range of 4.55–4.78% with a mild downward bias while stocks are under pressure; a stock rebound or hot data would bring 4.75% back, and a further slide would test 4.55%.
us2y.watch: 2-year auction early next week, Fed speakers and stock sentiment before Thanksgiving.

us5y.note: Down about 14bp to near 4.72%, with the belly rallying almost as much as the 2-year.
us5y.why: The 5-year fell with the front end as the S&P 500 dropped 3.7% and the Nasdaq 5.3%, and traders cut the pace of expected Fed tightening, unwinding 50bp bets while keeping a 25bp December hike. Lower UMich inflation expectations and falling commodity prices, from copper to gasoline, eased inflation fears.
us5y.outlook: Range of 4.62–4.85% with a mild downward bias; a stock rebound or firm data would take it back toward 4.85%, while deeper losses would test 4.62%.
us5y.watch: 5-year auction next week, Fed speakers and equity moves.

us10y.note: Down about 12bp to near 4.93%, back below 5% for the first time in weeks; the curve steepened.
us10y.why: Safe-haven demand drove the 10-year below 5% as the AI sell-off deepened, with Nvidia down 13.8% on an SEC accounting probe and the S&P 500 in a correction. Bets on a 50bp December hike were dropped and UMich long-run inflation expectations eased to 3.3%. The long end rallied less than the front as term premium stays high, steepening the curve.
us10y.outlook: Range of 4.85–5.05% with a mild downward bias while stocks are weak; a close below 4.85% would need further equity losses or weak data, and a rebound in risk would bring 5.05% back.
us10y.watch: 7-year auction next week, equity sentiment and holiday-thinned trading.

us30y.note: Down about 8bp to near 5.32%, rallying least as 2s30s steepened.
us30y.why: The long bond joined the haven rally but lagged shorter maturities: the market sees the stock rout slowing the Fed's pace, which helps the front end most, while heavy federal borrowing and inflation risk keep the term premium high. Lower oil-driven inflation expectations helped at the margin.
us30y.outlook: Range of 5.25–5.42% with a neutral bias; a further equity slump would test 5.25%, while a risk rebound or supply worries would bring 5.42% back.
us30y.watch: Next week's supply, equity moves and Fed speakers.

de2y.note: Down about 9bp to near 3.07%, tracking the global flight to safety.
de2y.why: Schatz rallied as European stocks fell, with the DAX down 2.6%, and the US front end repriced lower. ECB pricing eased a little but still shows about a 93% chance of a 25bp hike at the Dec 17 meeting and about 61bp of hikes in 2027. Lagarde spoke about wider swap lines, not rates, so there was no pushback.
de2y.outlook: Range of 3.00–3.15% with a mild downward bias while stocks are weak; strong flash PMIs or hawkish ECB comments would bring 3.15% back.
de2y.watch: Euro-area flash PMIs Mon Nov 23, ECB speakers and flash HICP Dec 1.

de5y.note: Down about 9bp to near 3.13%, in line with the front end.
de5y.why: The belly rallied with Schatz as the AI sell-off spread to Europe and US yields fell 12–15bp, pulling ECB pricing slightly lower. Weaker energy prices over the week also eased inflation fears, though a December ECB hike is still largely priced. The DAX's 2.6% drop kept demand focused on safe German paper.
de5y.outlook: Range of 3.05–3.22% with a mild downward bias; weak PMIs would test 3.05%, while a rebound in risk or hot inflation would bring 3.22%.
de5y.watch: Flash PMIs Mon Nov 23 and flash HICP Dec 1.

de10y.note: Down about 9.5bp to near 3.30%, the low of the week, and down about 9bp over the week.
de10y.why: Bunds gained as investors sought safety from the AI-led stock sell-off, with the DAX down 2.6% and 7.3% on the week, and as US Treasuries rallied strongly. The 10-year is now about 35bp below its 3.65% September high as lower energy prices ease inflation concerns, though ECB hike pricing and heavy borrowing limit the rally.
de10y.outlook: Range of 3.22–3.40% with a mild downward bias; a break below 3.22% would need weak PMIs or more equity losses, while a stock rebound would bring 3.40% back.
de10y.watch: Flash PMIs Mon Nov 23, German supply and US yields.

de30y.note: Down about 7bp to near 3.70%, rallying less than shorter Bunds.
de30y.why: The long end joined the haven rally but lagged as Germany's large borrowing plans keep term premium elevated. The fall followed US 30-year yields, which dropped about 8bp as stocks slid. The 2s30s curve steepened as the front end, more sensitive to ECB pricing, led the rally, and lower energy prices over the week trimmed long-run inflation worries.
de30y.outlook: Range of 3.62–3.78% with a neutral bias; a deeper risk-off move would test 3.62%, while weak auctions or a rebound in US long yields would bring 3.78%.
de30y.watch: German supply, flash PMIs and US long-end moves.

fr2y.note: Down about 7bp to near 3.57%, lagging German 2-year yields slightly.
fr2y.why: Short OATs rallied with ECB pricing as the AI stock rout spread to Europe and the CAC 40 fell 1.9%. The 2-year moved a little less than Schatz because haven buying favoured German debt, though fiscal risk matters less at this maturity.
fr2y.outlook: Range of 3.50–3.65% with a mild downward bias while risk is off; hawkish ECB comments or a firm HICP print would bring 3.65% back.
fr2y.watch: Flash PMIs Mon Nov 23, flash HICP Dec 1 and the ECB Dec 17.

fr5y.note: Down about 6bp to near 4.26%, retracing Thursday's auction-led rise.
fr5y.why: Middle OATs recovered after Thursday's €11.99bn auction cheapened the curve, helped by the global bond rally and lower euro-area yields. The move lagged Germany's as investors preferred Bunds for safety, and France's budget debate keeps a risk premium in place.
fr5y.outlook: Range of 4.18–4.35% with a neutral bias; budget progress would pull it toward 4.18%, while a government crisis or poor polls would lift it toward 4.35%.
fr5y.watch: Budget debate in parliament, presidential polls and flash PMIs Mon Nov 23.

fr10y.note: Down 6bp to about 4.87%, but the spread to Bunds widened about 3.5bp to near 157bp.
fr10y.why: OATs rallied with global bonds as stocks fell, but less than Bunds, which drew most of the haven demand; the German 10-year fell 9.5bp. In a risk-off market investors prefer the safest euro bond, and France's budget battle and 2027 election risk keep the fiscal premium in place. The spread is still below October's 176bp peak.
fr10y.outlook: Range of 4.78–4.95% with the spread at about 150–165bp; continued equity stress could widen it toward 165bp, while budget progress would tighten it toward 150bp.
fr10y.watch: Budget debate, presidential polls and the Dec 9 Senate vote.

fr30y.note: Down about 8bp to near 5.40%, still above the US 30-year.
fr30y.why: Long OATs rallied with the global haven bid as long French bond prices rose about 2%, recovering most of Thursday's supply-driven drop. They still yield more than US 30-year bonds because political risk before the 2027 election and heavy issuance keep a fiscal premium in the longest maturities.
fr30y.outlook: Range of 5.32–5.50% with a neutral bias; a credible budget path could take it toward 5.32%, while a political setback or a rebound in global long yields would lift it toward 5.50%.
fr30y.watch: Budget debate, presidential polls and US long-end moves.

watch: Next: euro-area flash PMIs Mon Nov 23; US 2-, 5- and 7-year auctions and EIA stocks early in the week; US Thanksgiving Nov 26; OPEC+ Nov 29; euro-area flash HICP Dec 1, then the Fed Dec 8–9, US CPI Dec 10 and ECB Dec 17.
